text:
marta (Support): FYI ACME just escalated — their chat app started returning much shorter, bland answers after our midday deploy. They say it got 'safer' and not helpful. Examples attached.

anna (Customer Success): Oof. Do they think we nerfed creativity? Any error logs or request_ids?

marta (Support): They sent a pair of requests. One from yesterday (good) and one from today (bad). Both to /v1/generate using model:redwood-alpha-2. No custom temperature/top_p in their app — they rely on platform defaults. Request IDs: req-ACME-9981 (yesterday), req-ACME-1123 (today). I'll paste the payloads and responses (redacted).

marta (Support): ````
# yesterday (expected)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-2","input":"Write a friendly onboarding email to a new user","max_tokens":180}'

# response: long helpful email, warm tone, ~150 tokens

# today (conservative)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-2","input":"Write a friendly onboarding email to a new user","max_tokens":180}'

# response: 3 short bullet sentences, very generic, ~30 tokens
````

sam (Eng Runtime): Thanks — that pattern (same payload, big diff in output entropy) strongly suggests sampling defaults changed server-side. Can you also paste the exact Response headers for the two requests (we need model-version, runtime-config, and any x-deploy-id)?

marta (Support): Attached headers: yesterday had `x-model-version: 2026-04-12-alpha` and `x-default-temp: 0.7` (weird but we logged it). Today shows `x-model-version: 2026-04-12-alpha` and `x-default-temp: 0.2`. Both used the same route and API key.

deploy-bot: deploy #deploy-8274 completed by @ci on 1869991005 - changes: platform-config/sampling_defaults.yaml (updated)

sam (Eng Runtime): Aha — deploy looks like it included a change to sampling defaults. I can see a PR that touched platform-config/sampling_defaults.yaml earlier: `default_temperature: 0.2` (previously 0.7). Tagging @oliver for rollout context.

oliver (Product): Who merged that PR? Was it intentional? We have customers relying on conservative defaults vs permissive defaults; we need a release note.

sam (Eng Runtime): The PR was merged by infra-ops during a config tidy. It looks like someone tightened defaults to reduce hallucinations for a set of internal testcases — but that change leaked into the global hosted defaults. Not gated by model or customer tier.

oliver (Product): That's a problem. Can we quickly revert to previous defaults for hosted-public routes and then push a scoped change if needed? Also need a cs message template.

sam (Eng Runtime): I can rollback the sampling_defaults.yaml to the prior value and redeploy the config. Quick mitigation: set global default_temperature back to 0.7 and default_top_p to 0.95, then restart route config. I will do a canary to 10% first.

sam (Eng Runtime): (after making change) Rolling back now — deploy #deploy-8276 created 1869991320. Canary to 10% of hosted traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy #deploy-8276 completed by @sam on 1869991329 - changes: platform-config/sampling_defaults.yaml (reverted default_temperature:0.7, default_top_p:0.95). Canary 10%

marta (Support): Sent ACME a note that we're investigating and asked for a short waiting window while we revert. They replied they can test in 5–10 mins and will confirm if behavior returns.

sam (Eng Runtime): For reproduction, engineering recommends they set explicit sampling params in the request to opt-in/out of defaults. Example to reproduce today's conservative behavior: ````
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-2","input":"Write a friendly onboarding email to a new user","max_tokens":180,"temperature":0.2,"top_p":0.8}'
````

sam (Eng Runtime): And to restore creative behavior even if defaults are conservative, set temperature 0.7/top_p 0.95 in the payload.

anna (Customer Success): Any impact on SLAs? We should inform customers who might rely on previous defaults. Also prepare a KB article: "Sampling defaults changed: how to pin behavior".

oliver (Product): Agreed. We'll draft a short postmortem note and a KB. Also adding a policy to require a config-change checklist + owner signoff before global default changes.

marta (Support): ACME just confirmed after ~7 mins: their app now returns the longer email again. They said they will keep an eye out and asked for the timeline for a root-cause writeup.

sam (Eng Runtime): I'll open a quick incident ticket and capture the PR diff, who merged it, and the timeline. Root cause: config tidy accidentally replaced global defaults; mitigation: rollback + restrict write access to sampling_defaults.yaml. Long-term: per-route defaulting and rollout approvals.

oliver (Product): Thanks. Assign action items: sam — incident ticket + restrict ACLs; marta — close after ACME confirmation and send CS note; anna — draft KB and customer-facing language.

marta (Support): Will follow up with ACME in 1h with summary. Closing internal thread when KB and incident doc ready. :thumbsup:
